case.title: Harden the EW RF Front-End Control Driver (VxWorks / Embedded C, Ada-adjacent)
case.brief: The provided context fits this role directly, so the exercise is built on it: you step in as a medior embedded engineer on an electronic-warfare receiver line. You are handed the existing memory-mapped control driver for the RX RF front-end (attenuator, synthesizer/PLL, power detector) that runs as a VxWorks task alongside an interrupt handler, plus its Interface Control Document, a legacy Ada built-in-test (BIT) package it must coexist with, and a test-procedure skeleton. Your job over ~1.5 hours is to add one control path, make the existing and new register access correct under real-time/ISR conditions, write a software test procedure that would actually catch the hard fault (not just happy-path), and produce a short decisions log plus a scope estimate against the program milestone. Assume any code you submit could be fully tool-generated — so what is being assessed is your judgment, your reading of the legacy material before you generate, your verification thinking, and the choices you make where the brief is open. The 1.5h is a hard cap; depth on the four tasks matters more than coverage. Keeping a decisions log (below) is normal engineering hygiene here, not a separate test.
case.repoSeed:
A small VxWorks-targeted embedded C/C++ module plus supporting documents for an EW receiver RF front-end control unit accessed over a local/memory-mapped bus:
- rf_frontend.h / rf_frontend.c — legacy Embedded C driver. Memory-mapped register block; functions include rffe_init(), rffe_set_synth(), rffe_read_power() (already returns a per-board cal-corrected value as signed 0.1 dBm using table g_pwr_cal[]), rffe_wait_pll_lock() (polls STATUS in a loop), and an interrupt handler rffeIsr() that services the power-detect interrupt and clears PWR_INT_ACK in CTRL. Runs in task tRffeCtrl.
- rf_frontend_ctrl.cpp — thin C++ control wrapper (per the role title) where new control entry points are expected to live.
- RFFE_ICD_v3.md — Interface Control Document / register map: CTRL (0x00: includes ENABLE, LATCH strobe, PWR_INT_ACK), ATTEN (0x04), SYNTH_FREQ (0x08-0x0C), STATUS (0x10, read-only: PLL_LOCK, BIT_FAIL, PWR_VALID), PWR_DET (0x14), BIT_CTRL (0x18). Section 4.3 describes the attenuation write + LATCH strobe but leaves encoding, settling time, and post-change PLL behavior underspecified.
- ew_bit.ads — Ada package spec for the legacy built-in-test sequencing (BIT_CTRL); its comments state the attenuator must be parked at REF_ATTEN before BIT runs.
- frontend_init.uml — UML state diagram of the init/calibrate/operate sequence.
- STP_RFFE_template.md — software test procedure skeleton with one example step and empty sections to fill.
tasks: Implement rffe_set_attenuation() (in rf_frontend_ctrl.cpp, calling into rf_frontend.c) to set the RX-path attenuation per RFFE_ICD_v3.md section 4.3 and integrate it with the existing init/control flow. Read rf_frontend.c and ew_bit.ads first — there are existing conventions you should not contradict.

Make register access correct under VxWorks real-time/ISR conditions. Your attenuation latch touches CTRL (0x00), which rffeIsr() also writes (PWR_INT_ACK); review that read-modify-write and the STATUS poll in rffe_wait_pll_lock(). Fix what is unsafe so it holds under interrupt load and compiler optimization, not just in a single-threaded smoke test.

Extend STP_RFFE_template.md with a software test procedure section that verifies rffe_set_attenuation AND is specifically capable of catching the concurrency/timing fault from Task 2 (i.e., a step a naive happy-path test would pass but the real fault would fail). State the setup, stimulus, and pass/fail criteria.

Keep a DECISIONS.md log: for every call you made where the brief was open, record what you chose, the alternative you rejected, and what you would have asked the hardware/ICD owner or the team. Then add a one-paragraph cost/scope estimate for hardening this control path across the remaining front-end variants against the integration milestone, with your assumptions and the single biggest schedule risk.

coverProbes.where: RFFE_ICD_v3.md section 4.3: ATTEN (0x04) + LATCH strobe in CTRL. The LSB encoding (e.g. 0.25 vs 0.5 dB/LSB and whether higher value = more or less attenuation), the required post-write settling time before PWR_DET is valid, and whether the synthesizer must be re-checked for PLL_LOCK after a change are all left open.
coverProbes.reveals: Good: candidate notices the encoding/settling/relock gaps, checks rf_frontend.c (synth path) and ew_bit.ads for an existing convention before assuming, picks a conservative interpretation, and documents or gates it as a question. Naive: hard-codes a plausible 0.5 dB/LSB with zero settling delay and no relock check, asks nothing, and ships silently-wrong RX gain that still 'compiles and runs'.
decisionSpace: Assume the conservative worst case (finer-step encoding, max settling delay, re-verify PLL_LOCK after the change) and document the assumption — safe but a slower control loop.
Mirror whatever encoding/sequence the legacy rf_frontend.c synth path already implies, to stay internally consistent — lowest divergence risk, but propagates any legacy error.

Treat encoding + settling as a hardware-owner question, stub the value behind a named constant with a TODO, and proceed on the rest — unblocks work now but leaves a gate that must close before integration.

coverProbes.where: rf_frontend.c rffe_read_power() already subtracts a per-board offset from g_pwr_cal[] and returns signed 0.1 dBm; ew_bit.ads documents that the attenuator must be parked at REF_ATTEN before BIT executes.
coverProbes.reveals: Good: reads the existing readback contract and the Ada BIT precondition, reuses rffe_read_power() as-is, and parks the attenuator at REF_ATTEN around BIT. Naive: generates a fresh raw-counts readback or re-applies the cal offset (double-correction) and ignores the BIT precondition, producing off-by-cal power readings and spurious BIT_FAIL.
decisionSpace: Reuse rffe_read_power() unchanged and honor the REF_ATTEN precondition — minimal and consistent, but couples new code to a legacy global.
Refactor the cal application into one shared helper both paths call — cleaner long-term, but a larger change than scoped and it touches Ada-facing behavior.
Keep raw counts in the new path and convert at the caller — flexible, but risks diverging from the established 0.1 dBm contract other modules depend on.

coverProbes.where: CTRL (0x00) holds both the LATCH strobe you must pulse and PWR_INT_ACK, which rffeIsr() clears; rffe_wait_pll_lock() polls STATUS (0x10). A single-threaded smoke test with no interrupt traffic passes.
coverProbes.reveals: Good: recognizes that a read-modify-write on CTRL races the ISR (lost PWR_INT_ACK), guards it (intLock/critical section, or restructures so the ISR owns the register), and marks the memory-mapped registers volatile so the STATUS poll isn't optimized away. Naive: emits `CTRL |= LATCH; CTRL &= ~LATCH;` plus a non-volatile poll — passes the shallow check, but drops ISR acknowledgements under load and can spin forever at -O2.
decisionSpace: Wrap the CTRL read-modify-write in intLock()/intUnlock() (or a spinlock) and mark the registers volatile — simplest correct fix, adds brief interrupt latency.
Restructure so only rffeIsr() owns CTRL and the task requests the strobe via a separate command/shadow register — lower ISR latency, but a larger architectural change.
Use a dedicated hardware strobe/test-and-set register if the ICD exposes one, avoiding the shared-register RMW entirely — cleanest if the hardware supports it, but needs ICD confirmation.

coverProbes.where: Task 4 estimate: the integration milestone date is blanked, the number of front-end variants is given only as 'the remaining variants', and whether Ada BIT changes are in scope is unstated.
coverProbes.reveals: Good: names the missing inputs (variant count, milestone date, Ada-scope), gives a ranged estimate tied to explicit assumptions, and surfaces the dominant schedule risk (cleared/Ada-skilled staffing, per-variant HW differences). Naive: returns a single confident number with no assumptions and no risk called out.
decisionSpace: Give a ranged bottom-up estimate keyed to an assumed variant count and call out the staffing/Ada-scarcity and per-variant-HW schedule risk — transparent and defensible.
Anchor to the one variant just completed and extrapolate linearly with a stated multiplier — fast, but hides hardware differences between variants.
Decline a single number until the variant list and milestone are confirmed and instead size only the first variant precisely — most honest, but may read as non-responsive to a program-cost question.
